issues.failure_explanation: The contributions list promises a bound on the operator-norm error between the estimator and A. The paper only bounds the operator-norm error to A_N and gives pointwise errors for a fixed f. The estimator is a finite-rank map on F_N, so for unbounded A it cannot converge to A in the D-to-F operator norm.

issues.overall_effect: Misrepresents the guarantee type: only pointwise (strong) convergence and error bounds to A are shown.
issues.title: Claimed operator-norm bound on the error to A is never established
issues.why_classification: The formal results are unaffected, but the advertised guarantee type must be weakened from a uniform bound to pointwise bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: Suppose the rate holds for every phi, even with a phi-dependent constant. Banach–Steinhaus applied to N^alpha(I-P_{F_N}) then gives ||I-P_{F_N}|| = O(N^{-alpha}). But ||I-P_{F_N}|| = 1 for every proper subspace F_N. So in infinite dimensions the hypothesis is never satisfied; the same holds for the D-version. The claimed constant, depending only on norms, would need exactly this impossible uniform rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts the error is at most ||A|| ||f||_D epsilon with probability p. The proof gives epsilon||f||_D + C epsilon||A||||f||, where C is an unspecified rate constant, and replaces it with '\lesssim'. Because ||A|| <= 1 in the graph norm, the first term alone can exceed ||A|| ||f||_D epsilon. The stated inequality is therefore not established; the hidden constant depends on C and 1/||A||.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound as (1 + C||A||)||f||_D epsilon, with C the rate constant, or rescale epsilon accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit probabilistic error bound is incorrect as stated, although the order in epsilon is unaffected.
issues.title: Stated error bound with constant 1 not delivered by the proof
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the constant preserves the rate and the method.

With the factor ||G_N^{-1}||^4 in the sample-size formula, M scales as epsilon^{-2-4/alpha} and the cost as epsilon^{-2-5/alpha}. The claimed costs, and their equality with the dense case, are therefore wrong.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The random variables $\set{(\bm{\eta}_N^m, \bm{\xi}_N^m)}_{m=1}^M$ have mean $\bm{0}$, are symmetric, independent, and independent of $\set{\bm{x}_m }_{m=1}^M$.
It can be seen that even when the error without noise is exactly zero (see Figure~\ref{imgOU}), the monomial basis functions are not resilient to noise.

issues.failure_explanation: With g = Psi(x) + eta, independence and zero mean give E[g g^dagger] = G_N + E[eta eta^dagger], not G_N. Likewise E[c g^dagger] = C_N + E[xi eta^dagger] and E[c c^dagger] = T_N + E[xi xi^dagger]; the assumption does not make eta and xi uncorrelated. The summands S^G_m and S^C_m therefore do not have mean zero, and the Bernstein inequality cannot be applied as done. As M grows, the noisy Gram matrix converges to G_N plus the noise covariance (about sigma^2 I for Gaussian noise), so the error does not vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either include the bias (noise covariance) in the error bound or assume known noise covariance and debias, and redo the concentration analysis around the biased means.
issues.overall_effect: The noisy-data error bounds and rates are false; the estimator is inconsistent under additive noise in the dictionary evaluations.
issues.title: Noisy Gram/structure matrices are biased; centring at G_N, C_N is false
issues.why_classification: The central guarantee (vanishing error with noisy data) is false, and no comparable version follows without new analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The conditioning event requires all M noise vectors to be bounded. By independence its probability is p_N^M, so only p_N^M P-tilde <= P holds. For unbounded noise such as Gaussian, p_N < 1, and p_N^M tends to 0 as M grows. The bound p <= p_N^M P-tilde[...] then fails for the large M that the lower bound on M demands, so the stated M-condition with log(4N/(1-p/p_N)) is unjustified.

failure_location.quote: Now, by definition of $\tl{\mathbb{P}}$, we have that $\tl{p}_N\tl{\mathbb{P}}\leq \mathbb{P}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conditioning with a union bound M(1-p_N) on the truncation event and choose the truncation level depending on M (about log M for Gaussian noise), or assume bounded noise; then recompute the M-condition.
issues.overall_effect: The probability guarantee for noisy data is invalid for unbounded noise, the advertised Gaussian case.
issues.title: Conditioning event has probability p_N^M, not p_N
issues.why_classification: A contained truncation argument restores a comparable bound with modified (log M) constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The joint vector (eta, xi) is 2N-dimensional, so sigma^{-2}|(eta, xi)|^2 follows chi^2_{2N}. The threshold gamma_N = 2N equals its mean, so p_N tends to 1/2 rather than 1. The chi^2_N tail bound used applies to only half the coordinates. The conclusion that noise has a small effect (a factor of 2) is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: As a result, we obtain that $\tl{p}_N\geq 1-(2/e)^{\nicefrac N2}\approx 1 $.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the chi^2_{2N} tail with a larger threshold (e.g. a multiple of 2N sigma^2) and recompute p_N and the resulting factor.
issues.overall_effect: The illustration of the noise bound's mildness is incorrect.
issues.title: Gaussian example: wrong chi-square dimension, so p_N is about 1/2, not about 1
issues.why_classification: This is a local recomputation in an illustrative example.

issues.failure_explanation: Each operator being bounded does not give a bound uniform in M, which is what is needed for a convergent subsequence of eigenvalues. Under only the continuity assumption (no i.i.d. sampling, no matrix convergence, pseudoinverse instabilities), the eigenvalues can be unbounded. Viewing f_M in F_N also needs the identification that holds only once the empirical Gram matrix is invertible.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $M$, $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ is bounded and thus the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{M})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume the base and moment assumptions for the first part as well; then the estimator matrices converge almost surely, giving eventual uniform boundedness of the eigenvalues.
issues.overall_effect: The first (existence) part of the theorem is unproved under its stated hypothesis.
issues.title: Boundedness of eigenvalues in M inferred from boundedness of each operator
issues.why_classification: Adding hypotheses already used in the second part is a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In many cases, however, $\Aa$ will \emph{not} be bounded (for example, if $\Aa$ is the generator $\Ll$ of the Koopman operator).
This is because the subspace spanned by the monomial basis functions is invariant under the Koopman generator of the OU system

issues.failure_explanation: Per-N boundedness gives no uniform bound. Counterexample: the OU generator with monomial dictionaries leaves F_N invariant, so A_N has eigenvalues 0, -1, ..., -(N-1). Choosing lambda_N = -(N-1), with eigenfunction normalised in D, gives a sequence with no convergent subsequence, contradicting the first claim.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, for each $N$, $\Aa_N$ is bounded. Thus, the sequence of eigenvalues $(\lambda_{N})$ is also bounded and has a convergent subsequence.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis sup_N |lambda_N| < infinity (or restrict to bounded A); the rest of the argument then applies.
issues.overall_effect: The dictionary-limit spectral convergence fails in the advertised unbounded (generator) case.
issues.title: Galerkin eigenvalues need not be bounded for unbounded A
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the hypotheses yields a comparable result covering bounded eigenvalue sequences.
